correctness.rationale: The exact four-index Hall inequalities follow by enumerating neighbor-set types. For primes >=5 primitive progression residues are uniform among nonzero affine coefficient pairs, each of the four roots has probability 1/(r+1), and a double root cannot occur. Inclusion-exclusion and a 12-bad-doubleton subtraction yield the formula. CRT plus Möbius inversion yields the H-asymptotic. Leading local base ratios yield the exact k-asymptotic constant 24. Exact Hall and residue enumeration and an independent occupancy dynamic program reproduce finite cases; no finite test is used to infer an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The exact same-bijection condition is strictly stronger than separate coprime matchings for each primitive progression. The directly motivating and foundational primary sources study single progressions, not simultaneous assignment densities. A separate previously established joint density for multiple divisor sets with a shared progression permits different bijections and does not imply the theorem. value.rationale: The natural first two-prime divisor lattice has four elements; asking whether a single matching works for k independently chosen primitive progressions is motivated by established single-progression matchability and is not answered by a family of separate matchings. The theorem gives an exact if-and-only-if criterion, a nontrivial full-k density, an explicit strict k=2 obstruction, and a sharp exponential constant 24, with honest scope limits.
